chief_complaint: feeling of a large ball or bulge protruding from vagina worsening after standing or lifting heavy objects
hpi_details: 68F G4P4 presenting with chronic pelvic pressure and visible complete herniation of the entire uterus and inverted vaginal walls outside the vaginal introitus (Stage IV Uterine Procidentia) requiring vaginal pessary placement or hysterectomy with apical suspension.
ideas: She thinks a heavy strain from lifting boxes caused a hernia or that an internal tumor is falling out of her body.
concerns: She is worried that the protruding mass is an advanced pelvic cancer, or that she will need a major operation that leaves her unable to live independently.
expectations: She hopes the doctor can fit her with a non-surgical support device to push everything back in so she can walk comfortably again.

teaching.diagnosis: Pelvic organ prolapse (uterine procidentia, Stage IV)
teaching.one_liner: 68F G4P4 with complete uterine and vaginal wall prolapse protruding outside the introitus.

must_ask.say: How long have you felt this bulge, and does it get worse with standing or lifting?
Do you have trouble starting your urine stream, or leaking urine?
Do you have difficulty with bowel movements or need to push on your vagina to pass stool?
How many vaginal deliveries have you had, and were any of the babies large?
We can discuss a supportive pessary device or surgical repair depending on your preference.

history.answer: I came in because it feels like a large ball or bulge is coming out between my legs, and it has gotten very uncomfortable to walk.
I first felt a slight bulge about two years ago, but over the last six months it has gotten much bigger and now stays out all the time.
It feels like a firm, heavy round ball protruding right out of my vagina.
It used to only come down when I stood for a long time, but now the entire thing stays outside even when I sit down or rest.
It feels much worse and heavier when I stand for long periods, walk around, or lift heavy laundry baskets.
Lying flat in bed used to make it slip back in, but lately it doesn't go back inside on its own at all.
I have a constant dull pulling sensation and heavy dragging ache in my lower pelvis throughout the day.
I feel like I cannot empty my bladder completely unless I gently push the bulge back up with my fingers, though I don't leak urine.
I often feel like bowel movements get stuck, and I have to press against the back wall of my vagina to pass stool.
I haven't seen any bright red blood, just a small amount of clear or pale yellowish discharge from rubbing against my underwear.
The skin on the bulge feels dry and rubs painfully against my clothes, but I haven't noticed any bleeding sores or open ulcers.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or sweating spells.
No, my weight has been steady and I haven't had any night sweats.
A doctor told me a few years ago that my pelvic floor was getting weak, but I didn't receive any specific treatment at that time.
I wash my hands and try to push the bulge back inside when it feels too heavy, but it pops right back out as soon as I stand up.
I don't have a cough, but I do strain when I'm constipated, and I do household chores and lifting every day.
It makes walking long distances and keeping up with housework very uncomfortable because of the constant rubbing and dragging feeling.
I gave birth to four children, all normal vaginal deliveries, and my largest baby weighed about eight pounds.
I went through menopause when I was fifty years old, about eighteen years ago, and I have had no periods or bleeding since.
My husband and I stopped being sexually active a couple of years ago because of the discomfort and this bulge.
I thought I must have ruptured something lifting heavy boxes or developed a massive tumor that is falling out.
I'm terrified that this bulge is an advanced cancer, or that I'll need surgery that leaves me unable to care for myself.
I'm hoping you can fit me with a support ring or device to push it back inside so I can walk normally without pain.
I do not have high blood pressure, diabetes, asthma, or any other chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries or hospitalizations other than when I delivered my children.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I do not drink alcohol.
I am a retired homemaker living with my husband, and I try to stay active around the house and neighborhood.
No one in my family has had severe prolapse, hernia issues, or tissue disorders that I know of.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/76 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 °C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Well-nourished elderly woman in no acute distress, walking slowly and moving cautiously due to pelvic discomfort.
Abdomen is flat, symmetric, and without surgical scars, visible distension, or visible peristalsis.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender throughout with no guarding, rigidity, or palpable masses; bladder is not palpable after voiding.
Normal female external genitalia with a large round mass protruding completely through the introitus.

Complete herniation of the cervix, entire uterine corpus, and inverted vaginal walls extending several centimeters beyond the hymenal ring (Stage IV uterine procidentia); exposed vaginal epithelium appears thickened and dry with mild erythema from friction, but no active ulceration, bleeding, or purulent discharge.
Normal resting anal sphincter tone; anterior wall bulges with laxity consistent with rectocele, with soft stool present and no rectal masses or hemorrhoids.
